read.says: Bloomberg News reported that Targa Resources is in talks to buy Kinetik and that a deal could come as soon as next week; nothing is signed and no price is reported. Kinetik closed at $54.70 on Wednesday and traded at $58.85 at 7:56 p.m. ET (+7.59%), just under its 52-week high of $58.90; Targa closed at $285.53 and traded at $280.48 (-1.77%). Blackstone holds about 48% of Kinetik and I Squared Capital about 19%. Kinetik is valued at about $9 billion against Targa's $61.24 billion; Kinetik owes $3.95 billion and Targa $19.8 billion. Kinetik was reported to weigh a sale in February and in September. On Nov 5 its management called asset prices less attractive than building its own plants. Kinetik is up 62% this year.

themes.beneath: The jump is small for a takeover. Kinetik traded about 7% above its close, just under its 52-week high (s5). My inference: either the market gives the talks modest odds, or it expects a small premium, because the price already holds two earlier sale reports this year (February and September) and a 62% rise (s5). Two owners hold about two thirds of Kinetik and can refuse a low price (s5). Against that, Kinetik's own management said three weeks ago that buying assets looked less attractive than building (s5). A note on size: the case file's $4.4 bn market value counts only the listed share class; the report values the company at about $9 billion (n:KNTK, s5). Last night's note pointed at Targa from the prices alone; the report now names it.
themes.cause: Bloomberg News reported that Targa Resources is in talks to buy Kinetik, with a deal possible as soon as next week; nothing is signed and no price is known (s5). themes.mechanism: A target rises toward the price a buyer may pay; the buyer falls because it may overpay or pay in new shares (s5). Kinetik's move is its own: the market and its drivers carried none of it (x:KNTK). The other pipeline companies it moves with did not follow: ONEOK -0.4%, Williams and Energy Transfer flat (p:KNTK~OKE, p:KNTK~WMB, p:KNTK~ET).
